pathway.title: CVR ENERGY INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage has improved through earnings, not repayment. CVR Energy's total debt including finance leases moved from USD 1,765 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,781 million at September 30, 2026, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 393 million to USD 919 million, taking gross leverage from 4.49x to 1.94x and net leverage from 3.19x to 0.55x. Because the improvement comes from the numerator, a normalization of crack spreads would move these ratios back toward the earlier levels, which is why the debt levels, not the ratios, are the steadier anchor. [Financial base; Business context, market drivers]

Second, the maturity and liquidity position is comfortable on a standalone basis. The February 2026 refinancing repaid the term loan, redeemed the 2029 notes and part of the 2028 notes, and moved the first principal maturity to 2028, when USD 733 million falls due (USD 183 million at CVR Energy and USD 550 million of secured notes at CVR Partners). Cash was USD 1,278 million and undrawn facilities USD 575 million, for USD 1,853 million, but USD 158 million of the cash sits in the consolidated CVR Partners entity and USD 500 million must stay unrestricted until the acquisition closes or the agreement ends, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline. [Financial base liquidity and maturities; Business context transaction summary]

Third, cash interest cover is high and well above the FY2025 level: trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 6.96x trailing cash interest of USD 132 million, against 2.77x in FY2025. This covers the debt as it stood, including notes issued in February 2026 at 7.500 percent and 7.875 percent; it does not cover acquisition debt. [Financial base interest cover]

Fourth, the pending acquisition is the dominant credit event. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, CVR Energy agreed to buy two refineries and related logistics from Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4.2 billion in cash. The committed funding includes a senior secured bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, a USD 550 million increase in the asset based loan to USD 1.1 billion, USD 800 million of convertible preferred stock from a commercial counterparty and up to USD 500 million from Icahn Enterprises. Because new debt is described as senior secured and the asset based loan is secured, existing unsecured noteholders would be effectively subordinated to a larger secured pool after closing. The permanent financing size, the target's earnings and total sources and uses are not supplied, so no post-closing ratio can be stated. [Business context transaction summary and gaps]

Fifth, claims outside debt and the definition of Adjusted EBITDA qualify the headline ratios. At September 30, 2026 the accrued RFS obligation was USD 230 million, derivative liabilities USD 160 million current and USD 18 million long-term, and accrued income taxes USD 132 million, none of which is in total debt, and the December 2025 contractual table showed transportation agreements of USD 995 million and purchase commitments of USD 165 million. Adjusted EBITDA adds back unrealized derivative losses of USD 278 million for nine months 2026 and removes favorable RFS changes, so it differs from reported trailing EBITDA of USD 964 million; the basis must be named whenever a ratio is used. [Financial base claims outside debt and definitions]

Sixth, governance is concentrated and in transition. Icahn Enterprises holds about 71 percent of the stock, the company relies on controlled-company exemptions, a separation and a new employment agreement for the chief executive are dated June 18, 2026, and the chief financial officer role is interim. Control is a funding positive, since Icahn Enterprises committed equity at the same price as a third party, but it also means transactions can be directed by one holder, and the legal protections for creditors sit in documents that are not supplied. [Business context ownership and governance]

cells.text: Diversified holding company in petroleum refining and marketing and, through CVR Partners, nitrogen fertilizer; two reportable segments in 2026.
Coffeyville refinery, name plate crude capacity 132,000 bpd, a full coking medium-sour refinery; Wynnewood refinery, 74,500 bpd.
Total throughput 227,637 bpd in Q3 2026 against 215,968 bpd in Q3 2025; 218,339 bpd for nine months 2026 against 169,848 bpd, the prior year including a Coffeyville turnaround.

Company gathering system and trucking supplied about 67% and 94% of Coffeyville and Wynnewood crude demand in 2025; a crude supply and intermediation agreement with Gunvor covered about 23% of 2025 crude purchases and runs to January 31, 2029.
Petroleum revenue is mainly gasoline and distillates; Q3 2026 petroleum revenue 3,135 against nitrogen fertilizer 146.
Bulk products sold to long-standing customers at spot prices off a Group 3 differential to NYMEX; rack sales at posted prices.
Petroleum top customer 12% of 2025 segment net sales; Nitrogen top two customers 28% of 2025 segment net sales; nitrogen contracts are generally fixed price and under one year.
UAN and ammonia were about 67% and 24% of nitrogen sales in 2025; Coffeyville facility uses pet coke, partly supplied by the refinery (about 36% in 2025); East Dubuque uses natural gas.
Petroleum first and fourth quarters generally weaker than second and third; fertilizer net sales higher in the first half.
Crack spreads rose from below to above mid-cycle after the Iran war began on February 28, 2026; management expects elevated diesel cracks until supply chains normalize.
RFS obligation accrued at 100% of the required amount for 2026 absent a waiver; the August 2026 waiver cut the 2025 obligation by about 253.
Net sold NYMEX diesel crack swaps outstanding; unrealized derivative losses of 278 in nine months 2026 are added back in Adjusted EBITDA.
Direct operating expenses per throughput barrel were 6.15 in Q3 2026 against 5.69; nitrogen direct operating costs include turnaround expense.
2026 estimate 220 to 240 in total; Wynnewood alkylation project about 155, expected late 2027; Coffeyville flare gas recovery about 53, expected late 2026; next Wynnewood turnaround in 2027.
Receivables, inventories and payables rose with commodity prices; accrued income taxes and the RFS obligation are new near-term cash calls.

runs.text: Strengths. Low standalone leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt of USD 1,781 million over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million gives 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, which leaves capacity to absorb a margin downturn before leverage returns to the FY2025 level of 4.49x. Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact): USD 1,853 million of liquidity, undrawn asset based facilities (USD 20 million of letters of credit issued against the CVR Energy facility), and no note principal due before 2028. Cash generation (Documentary Fact): nine months 2026 free cash flow after capital expenditure and turnaround of USD 872 million against negative USD 238 million in FY2025, which provided the cash build. Sponsor funding support (Analyst Interpretation): the Icahn Enterprises commitment of up to USD 500 million of equity at a third party's price aligns the controlling holder with closing and reduces the debt required. Regional logistics advantage (Documentary Fact): the company gathers about 67 percent and 94 percent of the crude for Coffeyville and Wynnewood.

Weaknesses. Cyclical, elevated earnings (Management Language carried, Analyst Interpretation on effect): management ties the margin improvement to the Iran war and calls the third quarter its best in company history; trailing figures include a quarter that is not a through-cycle level, so leverage is understated relative to mid-cycle. Pending acquisition (Documentary Fact): about USD 4.2 billion in cash, financed by new secured debt, a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion and equity of USD 800 million plus up to USD 500 million; post-closing metrics are Not calculable and secured debt would rank ahead of the existing unsecured notes. Regulatory and hedge exposure (Documentary Fact): an accrued RFS obligation of USD 230 million under court challenge, derivative liabilities and a large Adjusted EBITDA add-back for unrealized hedge losses. Concentration (Documentary Fact): two refineries in one region, one top petroleum customer at about 12 percent of segment sales and fertilizer top two customers at about 28 percent. Structure and control (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on control): about USD 569 million of consolidated debt sits at CVR Partners and its USD 158 million of cash is not freely available to the parent; the controlling holder can direct strategic transactions, and covenant terms are Not supplied. Management transition (Documentary Fact): chief executive change in June 2026 and an interim chief financial officer during a large transaction.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Pending acquisition. On November 2, 2026 the company entered into an equity and asset purchase agreement with indirect subsidiaries and affiliates of Marathon Petroleum Corporation to acquire the St. Paul Park refinery in Minnesota, the Mandan refinery in North Dakota, a 17 percent interest in each of Minnesota Pipe Line Company and MPL Investments, and associated wholesale marketing and logistics assets, assuming certain liabilities, for aggregate cash consideration of approximately 4.2 billion, subject to working capital and inventory adjustments. It is a Documentary Fact in the third quarter 10-Q, accounted for as a business combination with the company as acquirer, not closed at the cutoff, and a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Closing needs expiry of the antitrust waiting period and other approvals. Management expects closing before the end of 2026 (Management Language), while the risk factors state the outside date is 270 days after signing, extendable to 360 days in specified circumstances. A termination fee of 6%, 4% or 2% of the aggregate base purchase price applies depending on the circumstances; the dollar amounts are Not supplied because the base price is not separately stated from the cash consideration.

Financing. The company intends to fund the purchase with cash on hand, borrowings under its asset based loan, new senior secured debt (the permanent financing), the equity investments and the proceeds of a registered common stock offering. A debt commitment letter from Barclays Bank PLC and others provides a 364-day senior secured bridge loan of up to 2.5 billion to the extent permanent financing proceeds fall short, and consents to raise the asset based loan commitments by 550 to 1.1 billion at closing, or alternatively a new 1.1 billion facility refinancing the existing one. A commercial counterparty has committed to buy 800 million of non-voting common equivalent convertible preferred stock at closing. Icahn Enterprises committed up to 500 million of equity at the same price per share, terminating on completion of a common offering of at least 500 million. The company must hold at least 500 million of unrestricted cash until closing or termination, rising by up to 500 million of equity offering proceeds. Affiliates of the commercial counterparty will also supply crude, take product offtake and purchase initial crude and feedstock inventories at the two target refineries for ten years from closing, which is both a funding and a supply-side link. The size of the permanent financing, the total sources and uses and the target's earnings are Not supplied, so pro forma leverage and interest cover are Not calculable. The sum of committed sources cannot be compared with uses from the supplied text.

Creditor reading (Analyst Interpretation). Existing senior notes are unsecured; new financing is described as senior secured and an enlarged secured asset based loan ranks ahead of them on shared collateral, so effective subordination of the existing unsecured holders would rise on closing. Equity of 800 plus up to 500 reduces but does not remove the debt need. The 500 minimum cash and the bridge's 364-day tenor make the permanent financing market a near-term event. These are mechanics, not a view on outcome.

New debt issues in 2026. On February 12, 2026 the company issued 1 billion of notes, 600 of 7.500 percent senior notes due February 2031 and 400 of 7.875 percent senior notes due February 2034, with net proceeds of 993. Proceeds repaid the petroleum term loan, redeemed all 8.500 percent notes due 2029 at 104.250 percent of principal (a loss on extinguishment of 28 in interest expense) and redeemed 217 of the 5.750 percent notes due 2028 at par, leaving 183. On the same date the asset based loan was amended to raise commitments from 345 to 550, extend maturity from June 2027 to February 2031 and change the borrowing base and negative covenants. The effect was to push the first principal maturity to 2028 and to extend the maturity profile, with a changed coupon mix. The 6.125 percent senior secured notes of CVR Partners due June 2028 were not changed. Guarantee text for the new notes is in the 10-K and excludes CVR Partners and its subsidiaries.

fields.value: The financial base is usable. Reported statements for the annual report and the three 2026 quarters give consistent debt, cash and facility data, and the consolidated Adjusted EBITDA bridge ties to net income in every period checked. On a trailing basis to Q3 2026, gross debt is about two times Adjusted EBITDA, net debt is about half a turn, and cash interest is covered about seven times. All three are far better than at FY2025 because trailing Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, not because debt fell: total debt including finance leases moved little across the four balance sheet dates. The February 2026 refinancing cleared the 2027 term loan and the 2029 notes and pushed the first principal maturity to 2028. Three limits govern use. First, the ratios are on the consolidated perimeter, which includes the CVR Partners entity, its cash and its secured notes. Second, the trailing figure includes a quarter that management calls its best in company history, so the ratio shows capacity at current cracks and not a through-cycle level. Third, none of the ratios includes the pending acquisition, its bridge or its equity, and the target's earnings are not supplied. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

The RFS adjustment removes the 2025 and 2026 waiver gains (the 2026 waiver is described at about 253 and the 2025 waiver at about 488), so the measure is conservative on that item, but it also removes ongoing RFS revaluation. The derivative add-back of 278 for nine months 2026 removes mark-to-market losses on crack spread swaps while the derivative liabilities of 160 current and 18 long-term remain on the balance sheet, so a cash settlement against those positions is not in Adjusted EBITDA. The inventory valuation line removes a favorable 173 in nine months 2026 on a FIFO basis. Reported EBITDA, trailing, is 964 against 919 adjusted, and leverage on the reported basis would be lower, but the reported figure includes the waiver gains. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVR Energy is a controlled holding company with two operating legs. The Petroleum segment runs two mid-continent refineries, Coffeyville in Kansas and Wynnewood in Oklahoma, supported by crude gathering and logistics. The Nitrogen Fertilizer segment is CVR Partners, which the parent consolidates with about 37 percent of the units and all of the general partner. Earnings are driven by refined product margins against crude cost, by the cost of complying with the Renewable Fuel Standard and by fertilizer prices and plant utilization. The latest quarter was exceptionally strong, which management attributes to the conflict in the Middle East and to a regulatory waiver; both are external and reversible. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, the company signed an agreement to buy two refineries and related assets from Marathon Petroleum for about 4.2 billion in cash. The agreement is pending regulatory clearance, is to be financed by new secured debt, a bridge facility if needed, an enlarged asset based loan and preferred and common equity commitments, and carries a minimum cash condition and termination fees. For a creditor, the transaction is the dominant fact: it would roughly change the scale of the business, add substantial secured debt ahead of existing unsecured notes, and rests on documents and target earnings that are not in the source set. Governance is concentrated in Icahn Enterprises, which both controls the company and has committed equity to the acquisition. The standalone credit profile in the prior module is therefore a starting point, not the post-transaction picture.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pending acquisition. On November 2, 2026 the company entered into an equity and asset purchase agreement with indirect subsidiaries and affiliates of Marathon Petroleum Corporation to acquire the St. Paul Park refinery in Minnesota, the Mandan refinery in North Dakota, a 17 percent interest in each of Minnesota Pipe Line Company and MPL Investments, and associated wholesale marketing and logistics assets, assuming certain liabilities, for aggregate cash consideration of approximately 4.2 billion, subject to working capital and inventory adjustments. It is a Documentary Fact in the third quarter 10-Q, accounted for as a business combination with the company as acquirer, not closed at the cutoff, and a subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. Closing needs expiry of the antitrust waiting period and other approvals. Management expects closing before the end of 2026 (Management Language), while the risk factors state the outside date is 270 days after signing, extendable to 360 days in specified circumstances. A termination fee of 6%, 4% or 2% of the aggregate base purchase price applies depending on the circumstances; the dollar amounts are Not supplied because the base price is not separately stated from the cash consideration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing. The company intends to fund the purchase with cash on hand, borrowings under its asset based loan, new senior secured debt (the permanent financing), the equity investments and the proceeds of a registered common stock offering. A debt commitment letter from Barclays Bank PLC and others provides a 364-day senior secured bridge loan of up to 2.5 billion to the extent permanent financing proceeds fall short, and consents to raise the asset based loan commitments by 550 to 1.1 billion at closing, or alternatively a new 1.1 billion facility refinancing the existing one. A commercial counterparty has committed to buy 800 million of non-voting common equivalent convertible preferred stock at closing. Icahn Enterprises committed up to 500 million of equity at the same price per share, terminating on completion of a common offering of at least 500 million. The company must hold at least 500 million of unrestricted cash until closing or termination, rising by up to 500 million of equity offering proceeds. Affiliates of the commercial counterparty will also supply crude, take product offtake and purchase initial crude and feedstock inventories at the two target refineries for ten years from closing, which is both a funding and a supply-side link. The size of the permanent financing, the total sources and uses and the target's earnings are Not supplied, so pro forma leverage and interest cover are Not calculable. The sum of committed sources cannot be compared with uses from the supplied text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor reading (Analyst Interpretation). Existing senior notes are unsecured; new financing is described as senior secured and an enlarged secured asset based loan ranks ahead of them on shared collateral, so effective subordination of the existing unsecured holders would rise on closing. Equity of 800 plus up to 500 reduces but does not remove the debt need. The 500 minimum cash and the bridge's 364-day tenor make the permanent financing market a near-term event. These are mechanics, not a view on outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues in 2026. On February 12, 2026 the company issued 1 billion of notes, 600 of 7.500 percent senior notes due February 2031 and 400 of 7.875 percent senior notes due February 2034, with net proceeds of 993. Proceeds repaid the petroleum term loan, redeemed all 8.500 percent notes due 2029 at 104.250 percent of principal (a loss on extinguishment of 28 in interest expense) and redeemed 217 of the 5.750 percent notes due 2028 at par, leaving 183. On the same date the asset based loan was amended to raise commitments from 345 to 550, extend maturity from June 2027 to February 2031 and change the borrowing base and negative covenants. The effect was to push the first principal maturity to 2028 and to extend the maturity profile, with a changed coupon mix. The 6.125 percent senior secured notes of CVR Partners due June 2028 were not changed. Guarantee text for the new notes is in the 10-K and excludes CVR Partners and its subsidiaries.

fields.value: CVR Energy's standalone credit position is strong today, but the view for creditors depends on a pending debt-funded acquisition and on cycle-high earnings. The strongest support is the balance sheet at September 30, 2026: total debt of USD 1,781 million against trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million, or 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, liquidity of USD 1,853 million and no note principal due before 2028. The weakest point is that earnings are at a cyclical high from elevated crack spreads and regulatory waivers, while the acquisition for about USD 4.2 billion in cash, with a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, is not in any ratio. What decides the outcome is the permanent financing structure, the target refineries' earnings and whether current margins last.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage has improved through earnings, not repayment. CVR Energy's total debt including finance leases moved from USD 1,765 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,781 million at September 30, 2026, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 393 million to USD 919 million, taking gross leverage from 4.49x to 1.94x and net leverage from 3.19x to 0.55x. Because the improvement comes from the numerator, a normalization of crack spreads would move these ratios back toward the earlier levels, which is why the debt levels, not the ratios, are the steadier anchor. [Financial base; Business context, market drivers]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the maturity and liquidity position is comfortable on a standalone basis. The February 2026 refinancing repaid the term loan, redeemed the 2029 notes and part of the 2028 notes, and moved the first principal maturity to 2028, when USD 733 million falls due (USD 183 million at CVR Energy and USD 550 million of secured notes at CVR Partners). Cash was USD 1,278 million and undrawn facilities USD 575 million, for USD 1,853 million, but USD 158 million of the cash sits in the consolidated CVR Partners entity and USD 500 million must stay unrestricted until the acquisition closes or the agreement ends, so usable liquidity is lower than the headline. [Financial base liquidity and maturities; Business context transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, cash interest cover is high and well above the FY2025 level: trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 6.96x trailing cash interest of USD 132 million, against 2.77x in FY2025. This covers the debt as it stood, including notes issued in February 2026 at 7.500 percent and 7.875 percent; it does not cover acquisition debt. [Financial base interest cover]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, the pending acquisition is the dominant credit event. On November 2, 2026, after the balance sheet date, CVR Energy agreed to buy two refineries and related logistics from Marathon Petroleum for about USD 4.2 billion in cash. The committed funding includes a senior secured bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion, a USD 550 million increase in the asset based loan to USD 1.1 billion, USD 800 million of convertible preferred stock from a commercial counterparty and up to USD 500 million from Icahn Enterprises. Because new debt is described as senior secured and the asset based loan is secured, existing unsecured noteholders would be effectively subordinated to a larger secured pool after closing. The permanent financing size, the target's earnings and total sources and uses are not supplied, so no post-closing ratio can be stated. [Business context transaction summary and gaps]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, claims outside debt and the definition of Adjusted EBITDA qualify the headline ratios. At September 30, 2026 the accrued RFS obligation was USD 230 million, derivative liabilities USD 160 million current and USD 18 million long-term, and accrued income taxes USD 132 million, none of which is in total debt, and the December 2025 contractual table showed transportation agreements of USD 995 million and purchase commitments of USD 165 million. Adjusted EBITDA adds back unrealized derivative losses of USD 278 million for nine months 2026 and removes favorable RFS changes, so it differs from reported trailing EBITDA of USD 964 million; the basis must be named whenever a ratio is used. [Financial base claims outside debt and definitions]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, governance is concentrated and in transition. Icahn Enterprises holds about 71 percent of the stock, the company relies on controlled-company exemptions, a separation and a new employment agreement for the chief executive are dated June 18, 2026, and the chief financial officer role is interim. Control is a funding positive, since Icahn Enterprises committed equity at the same price as a third party, but it also means transactions can be directed by one holder, and the legal protections for creditors sit in documents that are not supplied. [Business context ownership and governance]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Low standalone leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt of USD 1,781 million over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 919 million gives 1.94x gross and 0.55x net, which leaves capacity to absorb a margin downturn before leverage returns to the FY2025 level of 4.49x. Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact): USD 1,853 million of liquidity, undrawn asset based facilities (USD 20 million of letters of credit issued against the CVR Energy facility), and no note principal due before 2028. Cash generation (Documentary Fact): nine months 2026 free cash flow after capital expenditure and turnaround of USD 872 million against negative USD 238 million in FY2025, which provided the cash build. Sponsor funding support (Analyst Interpretation): the Icahn Enterprises commitment of up to USD 500 million of equity at a third party's price aligns the controlling holder with closing and reduces the debt required. Regional logistics advantage (Documentary Fact): the company gathers about 67 percent and 94 percent of the crude for Coffeyville and Wynnewood.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Cyclical, elevated earnings (Management Language carried, Analyst Interpretation on effect): management ties the margin improvement to the Iran war and calls the third quarter its best in company history; trailing figures include a quarter that is not a through-cycle level, so leverage is understated relative to mid-cycle. Pending acquisition (Documentary Fact): about USD 4.2 billion in cash, financed by new secured debt, a bridge of up to USD 2.5 billion and equity of USD 800 million plus up to USD 500 million; post-closing metrics are Not calculable and secured debt would rank ahead of the existing unsecured notes. Regulatory and hedge exposure (Documentary Fact): an accrued RFS obligation of USD 230 million under court challenge, derivative liabilities and a large Adjusted EBITDA add-back for unrealized hedge losses. Concentration (Documentary Fact): two refineries in one region, one top petroleum customer at about 12 percent of segment sales and fertilizer top two customers at about 28 percent. Structure and control (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on control): about USD 569 million of consolidated debt sits at CVR Partners and its USD 158 million of cash is not freely available to the parent; the controlling holder can direct strategic transactions, and covenant terms are Not supplied. Management transition (Documentary Fact): chief executive change in June 2026 and an interim chief financial officer during a large transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis. CVR Energy's low standalone leverage and large liquidity support its credit today, but cycle-high earnings and a pending debt-funded acquisition under a controlling holder make the post-closing credit profile the deciding question (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.value: The evidence trace holds. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis handoffs was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and the three handoffs agree on every shared figure, period and perimeter label. The credit view of the synthesis, a strong standalone profile that is conditional on a pending acquisition, with Medium confidence, follows from its cited basis and is not overstated. Three points need wording care rather than correction. The headline liquidity figure includes cash and a facility that belong to the consolidated CVR Partners entity, and the synthesis mentions the cash but not the facility. The chief executive change is inferred from exhibits dated June 18, 2026 and from who is quoted in the April and July releases, not from a stated effective date. The unsecured status of the 2031 and 2034 notes rests on the guarantee wording, with the title of the 2028 notes stating it directly. No claim is unsupported and no contradiction between modules was found. The integrity verdict for the evaluated set is Restricted, not Committee Ready, because the conclusions that matter most to a creditor after the transaction, namely covenant headroom, ranking after closing and pro forma leverage, rest on documents and earnings that are not in the sources. The review itself is limited: it was done in the same session as the analysis, from the same extraction text, and page locators are extraction chunks rather than printed pages.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that nine-month 2026 free cash flow of 872 and trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 919 are real cash and earnings, that debt is little changed, that no note principal is due before 2028, and that the controlling holder has committed equity. The evidence against a comfortable reading is that the improvement comes from the numerator. What would make the supportive case win: a permanent financing and equity package that holds post-closing leverage near the standalone level, clearance of the antitrust review, and margins staying above mid-cycle through the first quarters after closing. Downside chain with observable triggers: the initiating condition is a normalization of crack spreads or an end to Middle East supply disruption, which cuts refining margin per barrel first, then Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow; the financial transmission is a return of leverage toward the FY2025 level (4.53x on current debt in the CP-2 sensitivity), with RFS purchases, derivative settlements and tax payments drawing on the 1,853 of liquidity; the refinancing consequence is the 364-day bridge and the 733 maturing in 2028. Triggers to watch: Group 3 crack spreads, RIN prices and the D.C. Circuit outcomes, antitrust clearance, launch and pricing of the permanent financing, and the covenant certificates once obtainable.
